answer: Each identity bonds 70 credits to one juniper cutting, decaying 5/epoch unless a fable refreshes it, proving one new work kernel ran, its hash matching the cutting's growth. Auditors replay the kernel log against the juniper registry; a copied or stale fable fails and the bond dies. Filing is 42; the k-th fake pays 42+7(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,538,500 plus 70,000 locked, pool 40,000. An honest agent files one fable for 42 and keeps its bond.
